articles.title: The Problem With Homeownership
articles.author: Michael Ledger-Lomas
articles.content_excerpt: A few days from now, my adopted hometown of Vancouver in British Columbia is going to elect a new mayor and council. The low turnout in municipal elections here skews toward affluent owners of detached houses who pay the most property tax and grumble about it. Mayor Ken Sim and his ABC (“A Better City”) party, who won the 2022 election, understand their base: they froze property taxes this year after abolishing the living wage for city employees. The ABC administration also implemented a wave of layoffs and promises to repeat the trick next year if reelected. Meanwhile, underfunding has left two-thirds of the city’s community centers to crumble away . articles.title: Western Thought Justified Animal Cruelty
articles.author: Ondine Sherman
articles.content_excerpt: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. At age seven, sitting at the dinner table with my family, I prodded my fork into a thick, squishy brown shape on my plate. My grandmother, who lived with us, had cooked her traditional Lithuanian-Jewish Litvak meal, and everyone had dug in. “ What is it? ” I asked. My beloved gran whispered back from across the table, “tongue.” I stuck out my tongue. “ This kind? ” She smiled. “ Yes, darling, but from a cow, not a little girl .” It was my first moral shock. Animals are our friends, aren’t they? Certainly, my dog Bronnie was, and all the animals in the picture books and animated films I saw as a child suggested this. articles.title: Student Protests Are Making Their Mark on Serbia’s Election
articles.author: Lela Vujanić
articles.content_excerpt: Sitting in the trashy garden of a café frequented by students near an iconic Belgrade market, we are, naturally, discussing the elections. A somewhat hippieish father of a friend complains that the situation is terrible, that he’s never seen such polarization, and that decades-old colleagues are barely on speaking terms. He tells me he tried to lighten the atmosphere, joking “Guys, I am neutral, you can relax, you can all be yourselves with me.” His remark didn’t sit well with either camp. Nobody in Serbia these days seems to like “neutrals,” though it seems that this despised group could decide the outcome of the October 25 parliamentary elections. articles.title: trumps american history
articles.author: Eva Amar
articles.content_excerpt: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. I have a confession to make, and I'm not particularly proud of it. Somewhere between middle school and high school, I decided history wasn't for me. It seemed like an endless parade of dates, timelines, and wars, interrupted by still more wars. I paid enough attention to pass the tests, but I certainly wasn't sitting on the edge of my seat waiting to find out what happened next. What did any of that have to do with my life? Well, seventy years of living have given me a rather different perspective. History isn't simply a collection of dates, wars, and presidents. It's our baseline. Without it, how can we recognize the warning signs of something we've already lived through?
